bridge: Builds on O03 privacy, S01 assets and G01 governance. Legal duties depend on jurisdiction and current authoritative guidance; this lesson is a design exercise, not legal advice for a live organisation.
teaching:
Privacy considers what data is collected, for what purpose, who can use it and when it is removed. Security protects data under a policy; collecting unnecessary data securely can still create a privacy problem. Begin with data minimisation and a clear purpose.

Human factors affect the real system. A control that depends on remembering an obscure procedure may fail under pressure. Design safe defaults, understandable recovery and messages that explain actions without revealing secrets. Test with learners using keyboards, assistive technology and different levels of prior knowledge.

Regulation adds jurisdiction-specific obligations and rights. Identify the relevant authority, role, processing purpose and retention basis before applying a rule. Record the date/source of legal guidance and escalate organisation-specific questions appropriately. A course completion record is not proof that an organisation has met every legal requirement.
example:
Fictional learning app
Purpose: save lesson progress across devices.
Needed: account identifier, progress and learner-authored notes.
Not needed: passport scan, family income, unrelated contact list.
Controls: private account access, export/recovery, explicit retention process.
Risk: learners may accidentally put real secrets in notes.
Design: clear nearby guidance and a way to edit/remove their text.
explanation: The app should not collect extra identity documents simply because a form could request them. Notes are user-generated and may contain sensitive material, so access, retention and deletion design remain relevant. A warning alone does not replace those controls.
exercise: Create a data inventory with purpose, access, retention and deletion/export considerations for the three needed fields. Redesign a warning so it states one clear action. Identify an applicable regulator for a hypothetical jurisdiction using an official source before making a legal claim.
solution: A good inventory separates required identity from optional display names and authored text. It contains no invented universal retention period. Guidance should be actionable, such as not saving passwords or private third-party data.
challenge: An app proposes mandatory passport upload solely to issue a self-study badge. Critique necessity and risk, propose a less intrusive design and distinguish an internal completion badge from an independently verified certification.
challenge_solution: A self-study badge can use a display name and transparent evidence policy without collecting government ID. An external exam provider may have its own identity rules. Do not misrepresent an internal badge as that provider's verified credential.
